newsitem.title: CHINA: China to auction bankrupt Haikou textile plant.
newsitem.headline: China to auction bankrupt Haikou textile plant.

text.p: China's southernmost province of Hainan will put up for public auction the biggest bankrupt enterprise in the province, the Haikou Textile Dyeing Plant, on May 8, the China Business Times said on Monday.

The auction would include the plant's working capital, its long-term investments, projects under construction, buildings, machinery and equipment, the plant's land use rights as well as vacant land and assets, it said.
The basic price was set at 130 million yuan ($15.7 million), it said.
The Haikou Textile Dyeing Plant was set up in 1986 with registered capital of 68.02 million yuan ($8.19 million) and total staff of 1,728, it said.

Due to bad management, the plant had been assessed to have total assets of 212.86 million yuan and liabilities of 361.98 million yuan with negative net assets of 149.12 million yuan at end-1996, it said.

Haikou city is one of China's 50 designated pilot cities for implementing bankruptcy of state enterprises. It has 43 state enterprises, of which 31 were making a loss and of these 12 had stopped production, China Business Times said.
The government planned to use either mergers or bankruptcy to deal with the loss-making enterprises, it said.
